elements.quote: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we assessed the clinical accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) of commercially available Ag-RDTs.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly labels the work as a 'systematic review and meta-analysis'.

elements.quote: we assessed the clinical accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) of commercially available Ag-RDTs.
elements.reason: The abstract gives a clear statement of the main objective/review question: assessing clinical accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) of Ag-RDTs.
The abstract evidence does not specify the main inclusion or exclusion criteria (e.g., participant types, study designs, specific eligibility criteria) explicitly.

elements.quote: We systematically searched multiple databases (PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, medRvix, bioRvix, and FIND) for publications evaluating the accuracy of Ag-RDTs for SARS-CoV-2 up until 30 April 2021.
elements.reason: The abstract lists the information sources searched and gives the date when the search was conducted (up until 30 April 2021).

elements.quote: We ... rated study quality and risk of bias using the QUADAS-2 assessment tool.
elements.reason: The abstract states the specific method used to assess risk of bias (QUADAS-2).

elements.quote: Descriptive analyses of all studies were performed, and when more than 4 studies were available, a random-effects meta-analysis was used to estimate pooled sensitivity and specificity in comparison to reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) testing. We assessed heterogeneity by subgroup analyses...
elements.reason: The abstract describes the analytic approach (descriptive analyses, random-effects meta-analysis, subgroup analyses) used to present and synthesize results.

elements.quote: From a total of 14,254 articles, we included 133 analytical and clinical studies resulting in 214 clinical accuracy datasets with 112,323 samples.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies, datasets, and the total number of samples (participants/tests) and summarizes study counts.

elements.quote: Across all meta-analyzed samples, the pooled AgRDTsensitivity and specificity were 71.2% (95% CI 68.2% to 74.0%) and 98.9% (95% CI 98.6% to 99.1%), respectively.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcomes (pooled sensitivity and specificity) and provides confidence intervals; sample/study counts are provided elsewhere in the abstract.

elements.quote: Across all meta-analyzed samples, the pooled AgRDTsensitivity and specificity were 71.2% (95% CI 68.2% to 74.0%) and 98.9% (95% CI 98.6% to 99.1%), respectively.
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted and the abstract reports the summary estimates with 95% confidence intervals.

elements.quote: Sensitivity increased to 76.3% (95% CI 73.1% to 79.2%) if analysis was restricted to studies that followed the Ag-RDT manufacturers' instructions. ... Testing in the first week from symptom onset resulted in substantially higher sensitivity (83.8%, 95% CI 76.3% to 89.2%) compared to testing after 1 week (61.5%, 95% CI 52.2% to 70.0%).
elements.reason: The abstract compares groups (e.g., IFU-conforming vs not; early vs later testing) and indicates the direction of effect (which group had higher sensitivity).

elements.quote: Concerns of bias were raised across all datasets, and financial support from the manufacturer was reported in 24.1% of datasets. Our analysis was limited by the included studies' heterogeneity in design and reporting.
elements.reason: The abstract briefly summarizes important limitations of the included evidence (risk of bias concerns, heterogeneity, and potential conflicts of interest).

elements.quote: Across all meta-analyzed samples, the pooled AgRDTsensitivity and specificity were 71.2% (95% CI 68.2% to 74.0%) and 98.9% (95% CI 98.6% to 99.1%), respectively. Sensitivity increased to 76.3% ... LumiraDx showed the highest sensitivity... Our analysis was limited by the included studies' heterogeneity in design and reporting.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results (overall pooled accuracy, variation by test and circumstances) and notes implications about variability and limitations.

elements.quote: We also completed the PRISMA checklist (S1 PRISMA Checklist). Furthermore, we registered the review on PROSPERO (registration number: CRD42020225140).
elements.reason: The abstract/methods sections report the register name (PROSPERO) and the registration number (CRD42020225140).

elements.quote: Initial data from independent evaluations suggest that the performance of SARS-CoV-2 Ag-RDTs may be lower than what is reported by the manufacturers. In addition, Ag-RDT accuracy seems to vary substantially between tests [4-6]. With the increased availability of Ag-RDTs, an increasing number of independent validations have been published. Such evaluations differ widely in their quality, methods, and results, making it difficult to assess the true performance of the respective tests [7].
elements.reason: The introduction describes the current state of knowledge about Ag-RDT performance and highlights important uncertainties and variability in evaluations.

elements.quote: To inform decision makers on the best choice of individual tests, an aggregated, widely available, and frequently updated assessment of the quality, performance, and independence of the data is urgently needed.
elements.reason: The text explicitly states the importance and need for an up-to-date aggregated assessment to inform decision makers, explaining why the review is needed.

elements.quote: While other systematic reviews have been published, they include data only up until November 2020 [8-11], exclude preprints [12], or were industry sponsored [13]. In addition, only 1 assessed the quality of studies in detail, with data up until November 2020 [7,11]. With our systematic review and meta-analysis, we aim to close this gap in the literature and link to a website (https://www.diagnosticsglobalhealth.org) that is regularly updated.
elements.reason: The authors identify existing systematic reviews, note their limitations (date coverage, exclusions, sponsorship, limited quality assessment), cite them, and explain how the current review fills the gap.
This review concerns diagnostic test accuracy (Ag-RDTs) rather than intervention effects; no mechanism of action of an intervention is relevant or described in the provided evidence.
The review is not of a complex intervention or delivery context and no logic model is presented or applicable in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we assessed the clinical accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) of commercially available Ag-RDTs.
elements.reason: The manuscript provides an explicit objective to assess clinical accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) of commercially available antigen rapid diagnostic tests, but it does not frame the objective using a specific question-formulation framework (e.g., PICO or another explicit structured framework).

elements.quote: As the COVID-19 pandemic continues around the globe, antigen rapid diagnostic tests (AgRDTs) for SARS-CoV-2 are seen as an important diagnostic tool to fight the virus's spread ... With our systematic review and meta-analysis, we aim to close this gap in the literature and link to a website (https://www.diagnosticsglobalhealth.org) that is regularly updated.
elements.reason: The review addresses diagnostic test accuracy for Ag-RDTs rather than intervention effects; therefore PICO-style planned comparisons for interventions are not applicable.

elements.quote: Weincluded studies evaluating the accuracy of commercially available Ag-RDTs to establish a diagnosis of SARS-CoV-2 infection, against reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) or cell culture as reference standard. We included all study populations irrespective of age, presence of symptoms, or study location. We considered cohort studies, nested cohort studies, case-control or cross-sectional studies, and randomized studies. We included both peer-reviewed publications and preprints. Weexcluded studies in which patients were tested for the purpose of monitoring or ending quarantine. Also, publications with a population size smaller than 10 were excluded.
elements.reason: The chunk specifies the reference standards, eligible populations, eligible study designs, inclusion of peer-reviewed and preprint reports, and explicit exclusions (monitoring/quarantine, sample size <10), covering the study characteristics used to determine eligibility.

elements.quote: At the end of the data extraction process, 37 studies were still in preprint form ... All studies were written in English, except for 2 in Spanish [175,280].
elements.reason: The review reports publication/report status (peer-reviewed vs preprint) and the languages of included studies, but does not specify any dissemination year restrictions or an explicit date-range for eligible reports in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: Reports assessed for eligibility (n = 266) ... Reports excluded: ... No estimation of sens. and spec. (n = 14)
elements.reason: The evidence lists exclusion reasons including 'No estimation of sens. and spec.' indicating exclusion due to outcome not reported; however, there is no explicit statement distinguishing exclusions because outcomes were not measured versus not reported across all exclusions, so the distinction is only partially addressed.

elements.quote: Wedifferentiated between clinical accuracy studies (performed on clinical samples) and analytical accuracy studies (performed on spiked samples with a known quantity of virus). Analytical accuracy studies can differ widely in methodology, impeding an aggregation of their results. Thus, while we extracted the data for both kinds of studies, we only considered data from clinical accuracy studies as eligible for the meta-analysis.
elements.reason: The review specifies the groups used for synthesis (clinical vs analytical accuracy studies) and states that only clinical accuracy studies were eligible for the meta-analysis, linking grouping to the review's synthesis decisions.

elements.quote: Also, publications with a population size smaller than 10 were excluded. Although the size threshold of 10 is arbitrary, such small studies are more likely to give unreliable estimates of sensitivity and specificity.
elements.reason: A rationale is provided for the notable restriction excluding studies with population size <10, explaining concern about unreliable estimates.

elements.quote: We performed the search up until 30 April 2021.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports the date when the searches were performed (up until 30 April 2021).
While bibliographic databases (PubMed, Web of Science, medRxiv, bioRxiv) are named, the search interface/platform and available coverage dates for each database are not reported.

elements.quote: We performed a search of the databases PubMed, Web of Science, medRxiv, and bioRxiv ... We performed the search up until 30 April 2021.

elements.quote: using combinations of subject headings (when applicable) and text-words for the concepts of the search question. The main search terms were 'Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Corona-virus 2,' 'COVID-19,' 'Betacoronavirus,' 'Coronavirus,' and 'Point of Care Testing.'

elements.quote: Two reviewers (LEB and CE, LEB and SS, or LEB and MB) reviewed the titles and abstracts of all publications identified by the search algorithm independently, followed by a full-text review for those eligible, to select the articles for inclusion in the systematic review.

Afterwards, data extraction and the assessment of methodological quality and independence from test manufacturers (see below) was performed by 1 author per paper (SK, CE, SS, or MB) and controlled by a second (LEB, SK, SS, or MB).

elements.quote: Two reviewers (LEB and CE, LEB and SS, or LEB and MB) reviewed the titles and abstracts of all publications identified by the search algorithm independently, followed by a full-text review for those eligible, to select the articles for inclusion in the systematic review. ... Afterwards, data extraction ... was performed by 1 author per paper (SK, CE, SS, or MB) and controlled by a second (LEB, SK, SS, or MB).
elements.reason: The screening step explicitly states reviewers worked independently, but the data extraction step describes one author extracting and a second 'controlling' without explicitly stating that the two worked independently. Thus independence is clearly reported for screening but only partially for data collection.

elements.reason: The methods state the process for resolving disagreements (discussion or consulting a third author), directly addressing how disagreements between data collectors were handled.
No text in the provided evidence describes processes used to obtain or confirm data from study investigators.
No information about use, training, or validation of automation tools for data collection is reported in the supplied evidence.

elements.quote: A full list of the parameters extracted is included in S1 Table, and the data extraction file is available at https://zenodo.org/record/4924035#.YOlzWS223RZ.

No explicit description of assumptions made about missing or unclear study information is provided in the supplied evidence. While the text notes that information was 'unclear' or 'not provided' for some datasets, it does not describe any assumptions the reviewers made to handle missing or ambiguous data.

elements.quote: We developed a study protocol following standard guidelines for systematic reviews [14,15], which is available in S1 Text.
elements.reason: The authors cite that they developed a study protocol following standard systematic review guidelines (references 14,15) and made it available as S1 Text, which serves as a referenced tool/framework that determined how data collection items were chosen.

elements.reason: The manuscript reports how many reviewers were involved in quality assessment (one author performed assessment and a second checked), that assessments were checked (indicating independent checking), and describes the procedure for resolving disagreements (discussion or third author).

elements.quote: We report point estimates of sensitivity and specificity for SARS-CoV-2 detection compared to the reference standard along with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using a bivariate model (implemented with the 'reitsma' command from the R package 'mada,' version 0.5.10). When there were fewer than 4 studies for an index test, only a descriptive analysis was performed, and accuracy ranges are reported. In subgroup analyses where papers presented data only on sensitivity, a univariate randomeffects inverse variance meta-analysis was performed (using the 'metagen' command from the R package 'meta,' version 4.11-0).
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly specifies the effect measures (sensitivity and specificity) and the statistical models used to synthesize them (bivariate model with 95% CIs; univariate random-effects inverse-variance meta-analysis when only sensitivity data are available).

No text explicitly reports thresholds or ranges used to interpret effect sizes (e.g., what constitutes small/large effect, clinical relevance thresholds) or the rationale for such thresholds. The document reports subgroup cutoffs (Ct and age) but not interpretive thresholds for effect size magnitude.
The manuscript does not describe methods to re-express synthesized results using another effect measure (no procedures or formulas provided for converting effect measures).

There is no explicit justification given for the choice of effect measures (sensitivity and specificity); the methods state what was used but do not provide a rationale for selecting these measures over alternatives.

elements.quote: If 4 or more datasets were available with at least 20 positive RT-PCR samples per dataset for a predefined analysis, a meta-analysis was performed. We report point estimates of sensitivity and specificity for SARS-CoV-2 detection compared to the reference standard along with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using a bivariate model (implemented with the 'reitsma' command from the R package 'mada,' version 0.5.10). When there were fewer than 4 studies for an index test, only a descriptive analysis was performed, and accuracy ranges are reported. ... We predefined subgroups for meta-analysis based on the following characteristics: Ct value range, sampling and testing procedure in accordance with manufacturer's instructions as detailed in the instructions for use (IFU) (henceforth called IFU-conforming) versus not IFU-conforming, age ( < 18 versus ≥ 18 years), sample type, presence or absence of symptoms, symptom duration ( < 7 days versus ≥ 7 days), viral load, and type of RT-PCR used.
elements.reason: The Methods explicitly state decision rules for which studies/datasets were included in meta-analyses (threshold of >=4 datasets with >=20 positive samples per dataset), that fewer studies would be described only, and predefined subgroup criteria; this describes the processes used to decide eligibility for each synthesis.

elements.quote: Weextracted raw data from the studies and recalculated performance estimates where possible based on the extracted data. The raw data can be found in S2 Table. We prepared forest plots for the sensitivity and specificity of each test and visually evaluated the heterogeneity between studies. If 4 or more datasets were available with at least 20 positive RT-PCR samples per dataset for a predefined analysis, a meta-analysis was performed. We report point estimates of sensitivity and specificity for SARS-CoV-2 detection compared to the reference standard along with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using a bivariate model (implemented with the 'reitsma' command from the R package 'mada,' version 0.5.10). When there were fewer than 4 studies for an index test, only a descriptive analysis was performed, and accuracy ranges are reported. In subgroup analyses where papers presented data only on sensitivity, a univariate randomeffects inverse variance meta-analysis was performed (using the 'metagen' command from the R package 'meta,' version 4.11-0). We predefined subgroups for meta-analysis based on the following characteristics: Ct value range, sampling and testing procedure in accordance with manufacturer's instructions as detailed in the instructions for use (IFU) (henceforth called IFU-conforming) versus not IFU-conforming, age ( < 18 versus � 18 years), sample type, presence or absence of symptoms, symptom duration ( < 7 days versus � 7 days), viral load, and type of RT-PCR used. In an effort to use as much of the heterogeneous data as possible, the cutoffs for the Ct value groups were relaxed by 2-3 points within each range. The < 20 group included values reported up to � 20, the < 25 group included values reported as � 24 or < 25 or 20-25, and the < 30 group included values from � 29 to � 33 and 25-30. The � 25 group included values reported as � 25 or 25-30, and the � 30 group included values from � 30 to � 35. elements.quote: This confirms prior data that suggested that antigen concentrations and Ct values were highly correlated in NP samples [16]. Ag-RDTs also showed higher sensitivity in patients within 7 days after symptom onset compared to patients later in the course of the disease (pooled sensitivity 83.8% versus 61.5%), which is to be expected given that samples from patients within the first week after symptom onset have been shown to contain the highest virus concentrations [298]. In line with this, studies reporting an unexpectedly low overall sensitivity either shared a small population size with an on average high Ct value [230,273,288] or performed the Ag-RDT not as per IFU, e.g., using saliva or prediluted samples [167,170,203,248,279]. In contrast, studies with an unusually high AgRDT sensitivity were based on study populations with a low median Ct value, between 18 and 22 [189,255,284]. Our analysis also found that the accuracy of Ag-RDTs is substantially higher in symptomatic patients than in asymptomatic patients (pooled sensitivity 76.7% versus 52.5%). This is not surprising as studies that enrolled symptomatic patients showed a lower range of median Ct values (i.e., higher viral load) than studies enrolling asymptomatic patients. Given that other studies found symptomatic and asymptomatic patients to have comparable viral loads [299,300], the differences found in our analysis are likely explained by the varied time in the course of the disease at which testing is performed in asymptomatic patients presenting for one-time screening testing.
elements.reason: The Discussion explicitly compares the review's findings with prior data and other studies (citing prior findings about Ct correlation, viral load timing, symptomatic vs asymptomatic viral loads, and specific prior assessments), thereby interpreting results in the context of other evidence.

elements.quote: Similar to previous assessment [7], the methodological quality of the included studies revealed a very heterogenous picture. ... The study may be limited by the inclusion of both preprints and peer-reviewed literature, which could affect the quality of the data extracted. However, we aimed to balance this potential effect by applying a thorough assessment of all clinical studies included, utilizing the QUADAS-2 tool, and performing a sensitivity analysis excluding preprint manuscripts. In addition, the studies included in our analysis varied widely in the reported range of viral loads, limiting the comparability of their results. To control for this, we analyzed the Ag-RDTs' performance at different levels of viral load. Finally, even though we are aware that further data exist from other sources, for example from governmental research institutes [303], such data could not be included because sufficiently detailed descriptions of the methods and results are not publicly available.
elements.reason: The Discussion explicitly describes multiple limitations of the included evidence: heterogeneous methodological quality, inclusion of preprints (potentially affecting data quality), wide variation in viral loads limiting comparability, and inability to include some external data due to insufficient public detail.

elements.quote: In this study we found that Ag-RDTs detect the vast majority of SARS-CoV-2-infected persons within the first week of symptom onset and those with high viral load. Thus, they can have high utility for diagnostic purposes in the early phase of disease, making them a valuable tool to fight the spread of SARS-CoV-2.
